clue.text: Wandering Nomad I Introduced into estate

indicators.note: the letter I is introduced into the shuffled letters, placed inside them
wandering letters stray from their places, so the word nomad is rearranged

explanation.surface: A roaming nomad is brought onto someone's landed property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wandering' looks like it describes the nomad, but it signals the rearrangement; 'Introduced into' then places the lone I inside the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is land owned or ruled by one person, as an estate is.

clue.text: Squeeze the last-drop: from the old sot?

definitions.text: Squeeze the last-drop: from the old sot?

parts.words: Squeeze the last-drop: from the old sot?
parts.note: wringing every last drop from something leaves it parched, and a drunkard who gives up the bottle goes through detox

explanation.surface: Wringing the final drop of drink out of an elderly drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: To wring a thing until no moisture remains is to dehydrate it fully, and an alcoholic in rehab is said to do the same.

clue.text: Supply all the details in form, if you must!

definitions.text: Supply all the details in form, if you must!

parts.words: Supply all the details in form, if you must!
parts.note: a bureaucratic form demands full specifics, so the instruction is to provide every one of them

explanation.surface: An exasperated official telling someone to fill in every box.
explanation.definitionFit: Particulars are specific details, so giving them is supplying full information.

clue.text: Infamously marked with a name for trading in

definitions.meaning: stigmatised, as a criminal once was burnt with a mark

definitions.text: with a name for trading in
definitions.meaning: bearing a trade name, as goods sold under a label do

explanation.surface: Disgraced and labelled because of commercial dealings.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand is both a burnt mark of disgrace and a trade name on goods.

clue.text: A lack of disposition to get on-well

definitions.text: A lack of disposition to get on-well

parts.words: A lack of disposition to get on-well
parts.note: two people whose temperaments clash cannot live in harmony

explanation.surface: Someone simply not inclined to be friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable to coexist harmoniously because of clashing natures is the sense of the word.

clue.text: Being mad about. No. I

parts.note: number one means oneself, so being crazy about number one is an obsession with self

explanation.surface: Someone crazy about the top of the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive obsession with oneself, 'number one', is a mania of self-regard.

clue.text: Nominated form for business accounts

parts.note: invoices from a firm carry a printed heading naming the company

explanation.surface: A designated form used for company bookkeeping.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed company heading on invoice paper names the business sending the account.

clue.text: Troop leader interrupting messenger man about the Palace

indicators.note: breaking into the messenger's word, so the letter sits inside it

parts.note: a courier carries messages

indicators.note: the leader of the word troop is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A soldier at the head of his troop cuts in on a dispatch rider near the royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troop leader' reads as an army officer, but 'leader' just takes the opening letter, which 'interrupting' sets inside the messenger.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtier is an attendant at a royal court, a man who hangs about the palace.

clue.text: Small measure of no great little drink

parts.note: a little great is its short form, G, as in GB
gin is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: A tiny tot of a modest little beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' here shortens 'great' to G, as in GB for Great Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A noggin is a small quantity of liquor, usually a quarter of a pint.

clue.text: A Red Cross bridge sparking

explanation.surface: A Red Cross team at a bridge where something is sparking.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric arc is a luminous discharge that leaps across a gap, bridging it with sparks.

clue.text: Revolutionary Corsican spirit

definitions.meaning: the French emperor from Corsica who rose after the Revolution
a grade of cognac brandy bears the emperor's name

explanation.surface: A rebel islander from Corsica with plenty of spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonaparte was a Corsican-born revolutionary general, and his name labels a brandy.

clue.text: The gold leafy part of the major Molucca bean

indicators.note: a part of the words is taken, a run hidden inside them

explanation.surface: Golden leaves found on a large tropical bean plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' points at the letters running across majOR MOLUcca; 'leafy' describes the foliage pattern in which this gilded metal is often cast.
explanation.definitionFit: Ormolu is gilded bronze or a gold-coloured alloy used for decorative mounts.

clue.text: Down payment on one's personal monogram?

definitions.meaning: the outlay made at the start of a purchase
a monogram is made of letters standing first in one's names, so money spent on it goes on those

explanation.surface: Paying a deposit on embroidered initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Costs paid at the outset are start-up costs, and initials are what a monogram shows.

clue.text: Hard water for the Scotch?

parts.note: frozen water is literally hard, and cubes of it are dropped into whisky

explanation.surface: A Scottish complaint about limescale in the water supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard water' suggests limescale, but here it means water frozen solid; 'the Scotch' is whisky, not the Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen water is solid, and it goes in a glass of whisky.

clue.text: What the liftman does to raise one's spirits

definitions.meaning: a lift operator carries people up

explanation.surface: A lift attendant's job is to cheer people up.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something higher, or to exalt someone's mood, are both meanings of the verb.

clue.text: It opens the door to empty houses for such children.

definitions.text: It opens the door to empty houses for such children.

parts.words: It opens the door to empty houses for such children.
parts.note: children whose parents are at work let themselves in after school with their own house key

explanation.surface: A key that lets kids into homes where nobody is in.
explanation.definitionFit: A door key for a sprung lock; latchkey kids carry one to get into a home with no adult present.

clue.text: Strangely. I've seen North from Strauss's city'

indicators.note: the letters behave strangely, ending up in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Someone surprised to have spotted the north from the waltz king's home town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' rearranges IVESEEN plus N. Johann Strauss, the waltz composer, lived in Vienna.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna was Strauss's home, so something belonging to it is Viennese.

clue.text: Ran into STD's twisted wires

indicators.note: one word goes into the other, inside it

parts.note: STD stood for subscriber trunk dialling, the old British direct-dial phone service; here read as a plural
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bumping into telephone dialling codes along tangled cables.
explanation.walkthrough: STD (subscriber trunk dialling) was how Britons once dialled long distance; here STDS holds RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Strands are threads or filaments twisted together to make a rope or cable.

clue.text: Neither Reagan's shown up

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown going up means the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: Ronald Reagan's short first name is Ron

explanation.surface: No part of Reagan is exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown up' reverses RON, Ronald Reagan's short name, in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The words pair as 'neither ... nor', each one introducing a negative alternative.

clue.text: Slip back into sickening ways

parts.note: falling ill again after recovering, or returning to bad habits

explanation.surface: A reformed character sliding back into nasty habits.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback after recovery is a falling back into illness or vice.

clue.text: He may help to clear litter from the battlefield

definitions.text: He may help to clear litter from the battlefield

parts.words: He may help to clear litter from the battlefield
parts.note: litter here is a carried bed for the wounded, not rubbish

explanation.surface: A volunteer tidying up rubbish after a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' looks like rubbish, but it is a portable bed for carrying the wounded.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical orderly carries casualties off on a litter, a portable bed.

clue.text: Cancel article in kiddies' yearbook?

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, inside it

parts.note: to annul is to cancel
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone scrapping a story in a children's yearbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the article inside the word for cancel. British children's annuals are hardback books, often based on comics, sold each Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's annual is a book issued once a year, often based on a comic.

clue.text: Live up to extremes of luxury in wicked style

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word live is read from the bottom
the extremes of luxury are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Indulging in a life of decadent luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses LIVE to EVIL; 'extremes of' gives L and Y, the first and last letters of luxury.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a wicked manner is acting with evil intent.

clue.text: Carbolic disinfectant left on messed-up phone

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it
the word phone is messed up, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A grubby telephone left to be wiped with antiseptic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messed-up' signals the anagram of the phone; 'on' means the letter for left comes after it in this across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbolic acid, an early antiseptic, is the chemical compound of this name.

clue.text: Northern territory I found in atlas, though it's supposed to be at the bottom of the sea

definitions.text: it's supposed to be at the bottom of the sea

indicators.note: these pieces are found inside the word atlas

parts.note: NT is the abbreviation for Australia's Northern Territory

explanation.surface: A map-reader spots a territory in an atlas, but the land itself lies under the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts the territory's abbreviation and I inside the atlas; the long definition describes the lost island of legend.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary island in Plato's story sank beneath the ocean.

clue.text: A starting price proving deadly when forked out

parts.note: SP is the betting abbreviation for starting price

explanation.surface: Betting odds at the off turn out ruinous when the money is paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forked out' sounds like paying, but it pictures a snake with its forked tongue out.
explanation.definitionFit: This small venomous snake flicks out a forked tongue and its bite can kill.

clue.text: The sort of chap Cato was, pouring scorn about small point

definitions.text: The sort of chap Cato was

indicators.note: the shuffled word goes about the point, around it
pouring the letters of scorn out lets them settle in a new order

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Cato, a stern Roman, heaping derision on a trivial detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pouring' rearranges SCORN to CNSOR; 'about' puts it around E, a compass point. Cato the Elder was a Roman censor.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato the Elder held the Roman office of censor, overseeing public morals.

clue.text: After Saturday I can't be gratified

parts.note: to be able is to be capable of doing, so can means able

explanation.surface: Someone who finds no satisfaction once the weekend arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan shows 'can' with a mark over it; the wordplay needs 'can', not 'can't'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something capable of being satisfied or sated is able to be gratified.
